text:
naomi: Follow-up from yesterday's active/active handoff sim. We saw ~800ms dual-primary on tenant X when control-plane jitter hit. Need a concise guardrail proposal.

rene: Quick recap: controllers A+B both attempted claim after transient partition; both accepted because TTL logic allowed it.

ops-lee: TTL was 1s, renew interval 250ms. With 250ms jitter and GC pause we can lose several renews.

naomi: Proposal: require two consecutive missed renewals before claim (hysteresis) + epoch bump and 409 on stale writes. Also expose a per-tenant handoff_mode: safe|aggressive. Default safe.

rene: +1. Also add metric lease.claim.attempts and lease.claim.success and a tag claimant_region.

sec-amy: Security/legal: ensure any cross-region write fallback records reason=(conflict|consent|capacity) in audit and retains for 90d. Manual operator overrides must be attributed.

ops-lee: Ops playbook: on repeated 409 across regions for a tenant -> pause cross-region routing for that tenant, notify on-call, and open incident stub.

naomi: Rollout plan: behind feature flag geo-handoff-v2, canary on control-plane test cluster with synthetic packet loss, then 1% traffic excluding residency-locked tenants. Rollback if lease.conflicts.count > baseline*2 for 10m.

deploy-bot: canary policy scheduled: geo-handoff-v2 -> 1% control-plane canary, monitors: lease.conflicts.count, write.409.rate, lease.renew.p95.

rene: One more: add controller /_lease_status endpoint exposing epoch and last_seen_ts for easier triage.

naomi: will update RFC with these decisions and link this thread. If anyone sees a gap call it out now.
